messages.author: cc1ef8c8158d6b73
messages.subject: Re: [knitr] knit_expand problem
parts:
In template.Rwn, use {{d}} instead of d:

\begin{figure}
<<{{paste(li[[d]]$title,d)}}>>=
ggplot(li[[{{d}}]]$data,
aes(x=a,y=b))+geom_point()+ggtitle(li[[{{d}}]]$title)
@
\end{figure}

Otherwise the variable d is not expanded to its current values in the
loop and will always take the last value when you knit() the expanded
source.

Regards,
Yihui

On Thu, Mar 14, 2013 at 3:34 PM, Ido Tamir <idom...@gmail.com> wrote:
> Hi,
> I am trying to access variables in a template with knit_expand, but
> something goes wrong.
> I would like to e.g. do something with the list of the parent environment,
> but its get expanded
> to the last value of the variable after the loop.
>
> When using {{ }} in the R-block I get: Error: Input to str_c should be
> atomic vectors
> ggplot({{li[[d]]}}$data, aes(x=a,y=b))+geom_point()
> ggplot({{li[[d]]$data}}, aes(x=a,y=b))+geom_point()
>
> thank you very much,
> ido
>
> main template ==========:
>
> \documentclass{article}
>
> \begin{document}
>
> <<run-all, include=FALSE>>=
> require(ggplot2)
> sl1 <- list(data=data.frame(a=1:10,b=1:10), title="item1")
> sl2 <- list(data=data.frame(a=10:1,b=10:1), title="item2")
> li <- list(df1=sl1,df2=sl2)
>
> src = NULL
> for(d in 1:length(li)) src = c(src, knit_expand('template.Rwn'))
> @
>
> \Sexpr{paste(knit(text = src), collapse = '\n')}
>
> \end{document}
>
>
> template.Rwn ===============:
>
> \begin{figure}
> <<{{paste(li[[d]]$title,d)}}>>=
> ggplot(li[[d]]$data, aes(x=a,y=b))+geom_point()+ggtitle(li[[d]]$title)
> @
> \end{figure}
>
>
